summary: A fairly quiet day: official Q3 growth figures arrive Monday, prices rose a little in September, and China's open AI models keep winning users abroad.
body: The big number is still to come. China's statistics bureau will publish data for the first three quarters of 2026 on Monday, October 19, at a government press conference[^1]. A Reuters poll of 50 economists expects third-quarter growth of 4.4% from a year earlier, up slightly from 4.3% in the second quarter. That would be just under the government's target range of 4.5% to 5% for the year. The same release will include September retail sales, a rough gauge of how much households are spending[^2].

Prices for shoppers barely moved. Consumer prices in September were 0.9% higher than a year earlier, a little below forecasts, while factory-gate prices (what producers charge businesses) jumped 5%, the fastest rise since mid-2022[^3]. Chinese state media says higher energy and industrial goods prices drove the consumer increase, while cheaper food held it back[^4]. Investing.com reports that household spending stays soft because of the long property slump, weak wages and a tight job market[^3].

On the tech side, Rest of World reports that new Western open-weight AI models (models whose inner settings anyone can download and run) still trail the top Chinese ones. Chinese models from DeepSeek, Z.ai, Xiaomi and Tencent hold four of the top five spots on the OpenRouter usage ranking, and experts say they can do some tasks 50% to 90% more cheaply than leading U.S. models[^5]. Separately, phone maker Transsion, little known in Canada but a big seller in Africa and South Asia, began trading in Hong Kong on October 15. It raised about HK$3.06 billion to fund expansion overseas[^6].

A daily-life story: Sixth Tone reports that many ordinary people who "sold" their faces to AI platforms this spring have earned little or nothing. AI short dramas mostly want celebrities and online influencers, and some users joined mainly to protect their likeness from misuse[^7]. My read: it is a useful reminder that a hyped side hustle often pays off only for a few.
differences: Sources stress different reasons for September's small rise in consumer prices. Chinese state media points to higher energy and industrial goods prices[^4], while Investing.com credits mainly holiday spending and says demand overall stays weak[^3].

reads.title: Western open-weight models still can't beat China
reads.summary: Why cheaper, downloadable Chinese AI models appeal to businesses and governments in lower-income countries, and what limits Chinese labs still face, such as shortages of computing power.
